findings.claim: Removing the `nodeParams !== emptyParams || (params && params !== emptyParams)` guard makes the key loop run unconditionally, so `handlerSet.params` now gets every `possibleKeys` entry explicitly set to `undefined` when no params were captured, instead of staying an empty object.
findings.rationale: With both `nodeParams` and `params` empty, `params?.[key] && !i ? params[key] : (nodeParams[key] ?? params?.[key])` evaluates to `undefined`, but the assignment still creates the own property. Callers that use `Object.keys(params)`, `in`, spread, or serialize the param object (e.g. `c.req.param()` returning `{id: undefined}` rather than `{}`) will observe a different shape than before. It also adds per-request work on the common no-param path that the guard existed to avoid. Additionally this was likely the last use of the imported `emptyParams` binding, which may now be unused and break a noUnusedLocals/lint build. Fairly confident this is a real observable behavior change.

findings.claim: Replacing the `processedSet[handlerSet.score]` bookkeeping with `!i` hard-codes the assumption that only the first `possibleKeys` entry may take its value from the incoming `params`.
findings.rationale: The rewrite is behaviorally equivalent today only incidentally: `processedSet` is re-created per outer iteration and `handlerSet.score` is constant inside the inner loop, so `!processed` is true exactly when `i === 0`. The new form bakes in an ordering dependency on `possibleKeys` and drops any expression of score-based dedupe (which would matter if `processedSet` were ever hoisted or handler sets shared). Worth verifying against multi-param routes where only the first key can be overridden by `params`. Medium confidence this is a latent hazard rather than an immediate bug.

findings.claim: `if (handlerSet !== undefined)` was weakened to a truthiness check `if (handlerSet)`.
findings.rationale: Any falsy-but-defined value (e.g. `null` stored in the method record, or an unexpected `0`/`''` shape) is now silently skipped instead of being pushed to `handlerSets`. The `as HandlerParamsSet<T>` cast means TypeScript will not flag a `null` here. Low probability given how `#methods` is populated, but it is a genuine semantic loosening introduced by this diff.
